# Summary of Cairn Mechanics

## Core Concept
A cairn is a stack that grows through pulses and shrinks through leaks and drains. The system creates interesting feedback loops where height influences growth rate.

## Pulses
When you pulse a cairn, it grows by: current height + stride + bonus.
The bonus equals how many complete stride-sized chunks fit into your current height (just count them, don't multiply by stride again).
Taller cairns get larger bonuses, so growth accelerates as height increases.

## Leaks
After pulsing, leaks cause immediate loss. You lose a number of marks equal to how many complete leak-sized chunks fit into your new height.
Unlike pulses, leaks always use the same fixed leak size and don't accelerate with height in the same way—they're a balancing mechanism.

## Drains
Drains are fixed losses—you lose the same amount every cycle regardless of height.
Drains work differently from leaks because they subtract a constant, making it possible for a cairn to eventually reach zero if the drain is large enough relative to the stride bonus.

## Repeated Pulses with Leaks
You must calculate each cycle one at a time because the height changes after every pulse-leak combination, which affects the next pulse's bonus.

## Finding Origins
To find what starting height leads to a target, you test candidates by pulsing forward and checking if you land on the target.

## Merging
Two cairns combine using weighted contributions. Multiply each cairn's height by its weight (which must sum to 1), floor each result separately, then add them plus a tether adjustment.
